instructions: Fill a large pot with water and bring it to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, husk the corn, pull off the silk and cut each ear in half.
Thinly slice the green onions, green parts and all. That should be about 1 cup. Put them in a heatproof bowl with the 1/4 tsp salt.

Heat the 1/3 cup oil in a small saucepan over medium high until a slice of green onion dropped in sizzles right away, about 2 minutes. Pour the hot oil over the green onions and stir. They'll sizzle and turn bright green.
Lower the corn into the boiling water and cook it for 8 minutes, until the kernels are tender. Lift it out and pat it dry with a towel.
Heat a large cast iron or heavy skillet over medium high for 2 minutes. A drop of water should sizzle off straight away.
Brush the corn all over with 1 tbsp of the scallion oil, leaving the green onions in the bowl. Lay the pieces in the dry skillet in one layer.
Cook them for about 8 minutes, turning them every 2 minutes, until they're charred in spots all the way around.
Transfer the corn to a plate and spoon the rest of the scallion oil and green onions over the top. Serve hot.
method_notes: All three versions brush or spoon a quick oil of green onions and hot neutral oil over corn charred on a grill. Cooking Therapy (the lead) boils or microwaves the corn first and chars it on a stovetop grill pan, Delightful Plate grills it from raw and brushes on the oil as it turns, and Vicky Pham adds a little salt and sugar to the oil. This uses a heavy skillet in place of the grill pan, adds the salt that Delightful Plate and Vicky Pham both use, and leaves out the lead's optional fried shallot garnish. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats, the trusted cook for this cuisine, has no version of this dish, so it leads with the best version read.
